policy_title: Reverse Unfair Increase to Family Visa Income Thresholds
stated: Reverse the Conservatives’ unfair increase to income thresholds for family visas, so that no more families are torn apart.

source.quote: Reverse the Conservatives’ unfair increase to income thresholds for family visas, so that no more families are torn apart.

bearing_set.reason: Family visa income thresholds directly gate the legal right to family life (Article 8 ECHR); reversing the threshold change determines whether lower-income residents can exercise that civil right or face enforced family separation — a genuine equal-treatment and civil-rights verdict.

Requiring a minimum salary to live with one's spouse/partner is a direct state restriction on family formation and personal choices; reversing it removes that coercive condition, improving freedom from state coercion over intimate life.

The threshold is inherently regressive — higher earners can sponsor partners, lower earners cannot; reversing it selectively benefits lower-income households, narrowing the income-based gap in access to family reunification.

membership_note: Three distinct non-negligible bearings: equal treatment (O9, disparate impact by sex and ethnicity), personal liberty (O10, state coercion over family choices), and inequality (O14, regressive access). Public-finances and prosperity effects are contested and too speculative to clear the non-negligible bar without further modelling.
